svg.title: What carried over between fields, and the two dates each transfer joins
svg.desc: Top trading cycles drawn for houses and for incompatible donor and patient pairs with a chain to the waiting list, a carried-over versus changed table, and a chronology of four method transfers.
svg.text: PLATE III-11-1
LIA / PART III / III-11 BETWEEN FIELDS
What carried over between fields, what had to change, and the two dates each
transfer joins
In none of these cases was the earlier work lost. The step was seeing that one problem had the form of another, then listing where
the forms part.
HOUSING MARKET, 1974
Top trading cycles
Each agent owns one indivisible house and ranks all the houses; there is no money.
Each agent points to the house they like best and each house to its owner. A cycle
closes, its members trade and leave, and the procedure repeats.
Green: a cycle that closes. Ink: an agent who waits for the next
round. The 1974 paper credits the procedure to Gale.
KIDNEY EXCHANGE, 2004
The same cycles, with a chain added
waiting list
patient
willing, incompatible donor
chain pairs
A chain ends at the waiting list: a patient trades the donor’s kidney for priority on the
list, an option the housing models lack.
Carried over
Had to change
Indivisible goods, differing preferences, no money.
Where every patient has a donor, the housing properties carry over essentially
unchanged, taking each donor’s preferences to match the intended recipient’s.
Patients without donors correspond to newcomers in a 1999 dormitory model, and
cadaver kidneys to vacant rooms.
A housing office knows which rooms are vacant; nobody knows which cadaver
kidneys will arrive or when.
Cycles were extended into chains that end at the waiting list.
Every operation in a cycle is assumed simultaneous, since a donor’s willingness could
change once the recipient has a kidney.
Context in the 2004 paper: more than 55,000 patients on the US waiting list; about 3,400 died waiting in 2002; selling an organ a felony under a 1984 law. Paired exchanges were proposed in 1986,
and a three-pair exchange took place at Johns Hopkins in 2003.
FOUR TRANSFERS AND THE TWO DATES EACH INTERVAL JOINS
rows share one time scale
Heat equation to option pricing
Fourier 1822
Black and Scholes 1973
151 years
solution taken from a 1963 textbook; the hedging argument is economic
House allocation to kidney exchange
Shapley and Scarf 1974
30 years
not a delay in performing transplants
Separation of variables, generalized
presented 1828, published 1831
6 years
Lamé and Duhamel presented analogous results in 1829
Citation analysis to web links
a large literature, no single year
Page et al. 1998
no lag stated
no descent from Leontief is claimed
Candidates written to the same pattern, examined by a dedicated skeptic
Seven killed, one surviving as an exploratory candidate: the Kibble-Zurek mechanism mapped onto opinion freezing. It fails on the voter
model and holds only on a majority-vote model; novelty is unverified and no novelty claim is made.
Sources: Shapley and Scarf 1974 via Roth, Sönmez and Ünver 2004, Kidney Exchange, Quarterly Journal of Economics; Black and Scholes 1973,
Journal of Political Economy 81; Kohn 2014; Page et al. 1998; Dictionary of Scientific Biography, Ostrogradski entry. Cycle drawings are
schematic; no case data are plotted in them.
